answer: Each epoch sells 200 identity slots by sealed bid. Bids lock in the ocean escrow, the prism ledger publishes the anonymized bid spectrum for recomputation, and a summit committee sets a 40-credit reserve and voids collusive bids. An attacker taking all 200 slots pushes the next clearing price up: prices run 40, 65, 95, 130, then 170 across five epochs, so 1,000 fakes cost 100,000 credits. A bid ring fails: identical low bids stand out in the prism spectrum, and voided ring bids lose deposits. An honest agent wins one slot at 40 once, while a faker pays more for every later batch.
